newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA MOVE AGAINST RELEASING INTERNATIONAL PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA MOVE AGAINST RELEASING INTERNATIONAL PLAYERS.

text.p: Barcelona have moved to alter rules governing the release of foreign players for international duty, and have encouraged other teams to join them in "correcting a very harmful situtation".
"The club...hopes that through its initiative it is possible to lay the foundations of a harmonisation of calendars and commitments," said a statement published on Thursday.
"Barcelona ...with a law firm ... have begun the necessary action with the Spanish and international football bodies."
FIFA president Joao Havelange has talked on several occasions of the possibility of creating a unified international calendar which would reduce tension between clubs and national sides.
The move comes just a week after Barcelona played a vital European Cup Winners' Cup tie without Brazilian striker Romario, who had gone home to play in a friendly against Lithuania.
Although the Spanish league calendar is generally suspended for national team games, clubs with large numbers of foreign players are routinely affected by international committments.

Only five members of Barcelona's first team squad of 25 have not played at full international level, while the number of foreigners has increased from five to nine in the wake of the European Union's ruling on workers' rights involving Belgian player Marc Bosman.
The communique said that the spirit as well as the letter of the ruling should be taken into account.

"...the Bosman case has created a new framework which has to be taken into account by the international football bodies so as not to prejudice the interests of clubs that have contracted, because of this new situation, (European) Community players."
